and be received as guests at court;
thus, five are called "emperor" concurrently,
and three are called "king,"
to manifest the five beginnings
and connect the three mandates.
Therefore, when the Zhōu people became kings,
they still honored Shénnóng as the Ninth Sovereign,
but changed the title of Xuānyuán,
calling him the Huángdì,
while preserving the titles of Emperor Zhuānxū, Emperor Kù, and Emperor Yáo,
demoting Yú but calling Shùn Emperor Shùn,
recording the Five Emperors with small states;
preserving Yǔ's line below in Qǐ,
and Tāng's line in Sòng,
with territories of a hundred lǐ square,
the rank title of "Duke,"
all having them wear their own attire,
practice their rituals and music,
and be received as guests of the former kings at court.
The Spring and Autumn Annals performs the duties of the new king,
altering the institutions of Zhōu,
aligning with the correct Black Sequence,
with Yīn and Zhōu as the descendants of kings,
demoting Xià,
changing the title of Yǔ to call him "emperor,"
recording his line with a small state.
Hence it is said:
"Demote Xià, preserve Zhōu,
treating the Spring and Autumn Annals as the new king."
Not treating the Marquis of Qǐ
the same as the descendants of kings;
why call him "zǐ" and also "bó"?
To show the distinction of a small state.
Why does Huángdì have a posthumous name first,
and the Four Emperors have posthumous names later?
It is said:
The title "emperor" must preserve five,
the emperor's generation heads the color of heaven,
the titles cycle back after five.
When the Zhōu people became kings,
Xuānyuán directly headed heaven with the yellow title,
hence called Huángdì;
the title "emperor" is honorable, the posthumous name humble,
so the Four Emperors received posthumous names later.
"Emperor" is an honorable title;
why record them with small states?
It is said:
The distant have honorable titles but small lands,
the recent have humble titles but large lands—
this is the principle of closeness and distance.
Thus, for kings, there are things unchanging,
things that cycle in two,
in three,
in four,
in five,
and in nine,
illuminating this connects heaven and earth, yīn and yáng, the four seasons, sun and moon, stars and planets, mountains and rivers, human relations;
those whose virtue equals heaven and earth
are called "Huángdì,"
heaven blesses and treats them as sons,
granting the title "Son of Heaven."
Thus, a sage king is called Son of Heaven in life,
after death is preserved among the Three Kings,
when demoted and extinguished becomes one of the Five Emperors,
down to attached states,
demoted to the Ninth Sovereign,
ultimately descending to become common people.
Having one is called the Three Dynasties;
thus, even if their land is lost,
their temple position and sacrificial animals are still arranged in the suburban honors,
revered in the generational temple.
Hence it is said:
"Their reputation and spirit extend into the void,
reaching longevity without end."
What is meant by cycling in two
and in four?
Why is Zhèng Hū named in the Spring and Autumn Annals?
The Spring and Autumn Annals says:
"Bó, zǐ, nán are one,
the wording has no derogation."
Why are they one?
It is said:
Zhōu had five ranks of nobility,
the Spring and Autumn Annals has three.
Why three in the Spring and Autumn Annals?
It is said:
The king's system
alternates between Shāng and Xià,
between substance and refinement.
The Shāng substance honors heaven,
the Xià refinement honors earth,
the Spring and Autumn Annals honors humanity,
hence three ranks.
Honoring heaven, modeling Shāng to rule,
its way emphasizes yáng,
cherishing kinship with much benevolence and simplicity;
thus establishing succession to the son,
being devoted to maternal brothers,
concubines honored through sons;
in marriage and capping rites,
naming the son after the father,
distinguishing the roles of husband and wife,
eating facing each other;
in funeral rites, burying separately;
in sacrificial rites, offering raw meat first,
husband and wife in separate Zhāo-Mù positions;
establishing three ranks of nobility,
two grades of official salaries;
designing suburban temples
and míngtáng as round,
their buildings lofty, solemn, and expansive round;
only sacrificial vessels round,
jade thickness nine fen,
white ornaments five strands,
upper garments large and high,
headwear solemn and round;
carriage canopy honored and covered,
modeling heaven's arranged images,
hanging four bells,
music with suspended drums,
using xī dances,
dance movements overflowing round;
first presenting hair and blood, then using music;
in penal law, much concealment,
among relatives, much avoidance;
fēng and shàn sacrifices at the elevated position.
Honoring earth, modeling Xià to rule,
its way advances yīn,
honoring honor with much righteousness and restraint;
thus establishing succession to the grandson,
being devoted to the heir,
concubines not called honored through sons;
in marriage and capping rites,
naming the son after the mother,
distinguishing the roles of husband and wife,
eating sitting together;
in funeral rites, burying together;
in sacrificial rites, offering cooked food first,
wife following husband in Zhāo-Mù positions;
establishing five ranks of nobility,
three grades of official salaries;
designing suburban temples
and míngtáng as square,
their buildings low and humble square;
sacrificial vessels square,
jade thickness eight fen,
white ornaments four strands,
lower garments large and low,
headwear humble and retiring;
carriage canopy low,
modeling earth's encompassing images carried,
hanging two bells;
music with set drums,
using xiānshī dances,
dance movements overflowing square;
first cooking, then using music;
penal law following heaven's model,
fēng and shàn sacrifices at the lower position.
Honoring heaven, modeling substance to rule,
its way emphasizes yáng,
cherishing kinship with much substantial love.
Therefore, establishing the heir and bestowing it upon the son,
honoring the full brothers,
and the concubine gaining status through her son.
The rituals of marriage and capping,
naming the son after the father,
distinguishing the roles of husband and wife,
sitting opposite each other to eat;
in funeral rites, burying separately,
in sacrificial rites, offering millet first,
husband and wife positioned separately in the ancestral order;
establishing three ranks of nobility,
two grades of official salaries;
designing the suburban temple,
the Mingtáng round inside and oval outside,
its roof curved like leaning elegance, oval in shape,
sacrificial vessels oval.
Jade seven fen thick,
white silk with three strands;
robes long with front lapels,
headwear round and revolving.
The imperial carriage with a revered canopy,
arrayed with celestial symbols,
hanging four bells.
Music with drum stands,
using feather flutes in dance,
the dance overflowing in oval form,
first using jade sounds then cooking;
in criminal law, much concealment,
many pardons for relatives;
the altar enfeoffed on the left.
Governing earth, emulating patterns to rule,
its way advances the yin,
honoring honor with abundant ritual refinement.
Hence establishing the heir for descendants,
honoring the eldest son,
the concubine not titled noble through her son;
the rituals of marriage and capping,
naming the son after the mother,
distinguishing the roles of husband and wife,
sitting together to eat;
in funeral rites, burying together,
in sacrificial rites, offering fragrant wine first,
the wife following the husband in ancestral order;
establishing five ranks of nobility,
three grades of official salaries;
designing the suburban temple,
the Mingtáng square inside and balanced outside,
its roof layered and balanced,
sacrificial vessels balanced and uniform,
creating orderly mechanisms,
jade six fen thick,
white silk with three strands;
robes long with back lapels,
headwear layered with hanging tassels.
The imperial carriage humble,
arrayed with earthly symbols all around,
hanging two bells.
Music with suspended drums,
using the "Ten Thousand Dances",
the dance overflowing in balance.
First cooking then using music,
in criminal law, public documentation,
the altar enfeoffed on the left.
The four methods cultivated from tradition,
originating from the former emperors,
thus the four methods are like the four seasons,
ending and beginning anew,
exhausted then returning to the root,
the heaven of the four methods,
bestowing signs and receiving the sage's kingly laws,
then life and form manifest in the ancestors,
greatly illuminating in the kingly ruler.
Thus when Heaven was to bestow upon Shùn,
governing heaven, emulating the Shāng to rule,
his ancestor was granted the surname Yáo.
Shùn’s physique was lofty with a round head,
and bright with two pupils,
his nature adept in astronomy,
pure in filial piety and kindness.
When Heaven was to bestow upon Yǔ,
governing earth, emulating the Xià to rule,
his ancestor was granted the surname Sì.
Yǔ was born from the back,
his body tall,
long-legged and swift,
walking quickly with the left foot first,
followed by the right,
laboring the left and resting the right,
his nature adept in action,
familiar with earth and understanding water.
When Heaven was to bestow upon Tāng,
governing heaven, emulating substance to rule,
his ancestor was granted the surname Zǐ.
It is said that Qìe’s mother swallowed a black bird's egg and gave birth to Qìe,
Qìe first emerged from the chest,
his nature adept in human relations.
As for Tāng,
his body was tall and slender,
left foot flat and right nimble,
laboring the right and resting the left,
his nature adept in heavenly light,
substantial, straightforward, and purely benevolent.
When Heaven was to bestow upon King Wén,
governing earth, emulating patterns to rule,
his ancestor was granted the surname Jī.
It is said that Hòu Jì’s mother Jiāng Yuán stepped on a heavenly footprint and gave birth to Hòu Jì,
Hòu Jì grew up in Tái soil,
sowing the five grains,
and by King Wén’s time,
his physique was broad and tall,
with four nipples and large feet,
his nature adept in earthly patterns and potentials.
Thus the emperor sent Yǔ and Gāo to discuss surnames,
knowing the virtue of Yīn,
a yang virtue,
hence the surname Zǐ;
knowing the virtue of Zhōu,
a yin virtue,
hence the surname Jī;
thus the Yīn king altered the script,
writing began with male,
the Zhōu king wrote Jī with female.
Therefore, the way of heaven moves each according to its kind,
who but a sage can understand it!
"The Official System Mirroring Heaven: Chapter Twenty-Four"
The king establishes officials:
three dukes, nine ministers, twenty-seven senior officials, and eighty-one scholars,
totaling one hundred twenty individuals,
thus completing the array of ministers.
I have heard that the model and method adopted by the sage kings,
the great principles of heaven,
are formed by three beginnings
and conclude through four cycles,
and the official system is likewise—
is this its model?
Three individuals form one selection,
modeled after three months making one season;
four selections complete it,
modeled after the four seasons concluding the year.
The three dukes are what the king relies upon to sustain himself;
heaven completes things in threes,
the king sustains himself with threes,
establishing fixed numbers as pillars,
and quadrupling them,
so that there may be no error.
Preparing the numbers of heaven to participate in affairs
reflects the intention of governing cautiously in accordance with the Way.
These one hundred twenty ministers
are all those with whom the former kings walked the straight path.
Therefore, the Son of Heaven triples himself with the three dukes,
the three dukes triple themselves with the nine ministers,
the nine ministers triple themselves with the three senior officials,
the three senior officials triple themselves with the three scholars;
three persons form a selection, quadrupled,
following the way of three to govern the world,
like the fourfold structure of heaven,
following the threefold time to begin and end the year.
One yang with three—
is it not the threefold time?
And heaven quadruples it—
their numbers are the same.
Heaven has four seasons,
each season three months;
the king has four selections,
each selection three ministers;
thus there are the first, middle, and last,
representing the nature of one season;
there are upper, lower, and middle,
representing the nature of one selection;
three ministers form one selection,
four selections complete it,
exhausting human circumstances.
Human talent inherently has four selections,
just as heaven's seasons inherently have four changes;
sages form one selection,
gentlemen form one selection,
good persons form one selection,
upright persons form one selection;
below these,
they are not worthy of selection;
within the four selections,
each has its gradations;
thus heaven selects four embankments,
twelve, and human variations are exhausted;
exhausting human variations and uniting them with heaven
can only be done by the sage,
thereby establishing royal affairs.
What are the great principles of heaven?
Three beginnings form a day,
three days form a cycle,
three ten-day periods form a month,
three months form a season,
three seasons accomplish a task;
cold, heat, and harmony,
three complete things;
sun, moon, and stars,
three produce light;
heaven, earth, and humanity,
three complete virtue;
from this perspective,
three form one completion,
this is heaven's great principle,
taking this as heaven's system.
Thus, in rites, three deferrals form one section,
in officials, three persons form one selection;
the three dukes form one selection,
the three ministers form one selection,
the three senior officials form one selection,
the three scholars form one selection,
totaling four selections.
Three ministers correspond to heaven's system,
altogether the three months of the four seasons.
Therefore, using three as a selection
draws from heaven's principles;
using four as a system
draws from heaven's seasons;
using twelve ministers as one strand
draws from the year's measure;
stopping at ten strands
draws from heaven's beginnings.
What are heaven's beginnings?
It is said:
Heaven has ten beginnings,
ten beginnings complete it;
heaven is one beginning,
earth is one beginning,
yin is one beginning,
yáng is one beginning,
fire is one beginning,
metal is one beginning,
wood is one beginning,
water is one beginning,
earth (as element) is one beginning,
humanity is one beginning,
altogether ten beginnings complete it,
this is heaven's number.
Heaven's number concludes at ten;
the king receives ten beginnings from heaven
and organizes them into strands by proportion.
Each strand with one beginning corresponds to twelve periods,
just as heaven concludes one year with twelve months;
ten is heaven's number,
twelve is the year's measure;
using the year's measure
to strand heaven's number,
twelve completes heaven's number.
Thus, ending ten years uses one hundred twenty months,
stranding ten beginnings also uses one hundred twenty ministers;
applying the proportion,
all harmonize with heaven.
The proportion is three ministers forming one caution,
so eighty-one scholars form twenty-seven cautions
to support the twenty-seven senior officials;
twenty-seven senior officials form nine cautions
to support the nine ministers;
nine ministers form three cautions
to support the three dukes;
three dukes form one caution
to support the Son of Heaven.
The Son of Heaven accumulates forty cautions to form four selections,
each selection one caution with three ministers,
all being heaven's numbers.
Therefore, calculating by four selections,
each selection has thirty persons,
three times four is twelve,
one hundred twenty persons,
also heaven's number;
with ten beginnings and four selections,
ten beginnings accumulate forty cautions,
each caution three ministers,
three times four is twelve,
one hundred twenty persons,
also heaven's number;
calculating by the three dukes' efforts,
each duke has forty persons,
three times four is twelve,
one hundred twenty persons,
also heaven's number.
Thus, dispersed and named, they are the one hundred twenty ministers;
selected and honored, they are the twelve leaders;
though named variously,
none is better called four selections and twelve leaders;
yet calculating them separately,
all have correspondences,
none missing heaven's numbers.
To seek the subtleties of heaven's numbers,
none is better than humanity.
The human body has four limbs,
each limb has three sections,
three times four is twelve,
twelve sections support each other,
and the physical form is established.
Heaven has four seasons,
each season has three months,
three times four is twelve,
twelve months succeed each other and the year's count concludes;
officials have four selections,
each selection has three persons,
three times four is twelve,
twelve ministers participate together and governance is accomplished;
from this, it is seen that heaven's numbers,
humanity's form,
and the official system
mutually correspond and harmonize.
Humanity and heaven
have many such correspondences,
all subtle and minute,
which must not be overlooked.
The principle of heaven and earth
divides the changes of one year into four seasons;
the four seasons are also heaven's four selections.
Thus, spring is the selection of lesser yáng,
summer is the selection of greater yáng,
autumn is the selection of lesser yīn,
winter is the selection of greater yīn.
Within the four selections, each has first, middle, and last,
so within selections there are selections;
thus, within one year there are four seasons,
within one season there are three leaders,
this is heaven's rhythm.
Humanity is born of heaven
and embodies heaven's rhythm,
thus also having variations of size, thickness, and thinness—
this is humanity's qì.
The former kings, following humanity's qì,
and divides its variations into four selections,
thus the positions of the Three Dukes
are the choices of the sages.
The positions of the Three Ministers
are the choices of the noble persons;
the positions of the Three Great Officers
are the choices of the good persons;
the positions of the Three Scholars
are the choices of the upright.
Dividing human variations into four selections,
selecting and establishing three ministers each,
is like Heaven dividing the year's changes into four seasons,
each season having three segments;
Heaven uses the selections of the four seasons
to harmonize with the twelve segments and complete the year,
the king uses the selections of the four positions
to sharpen with the twelve ministers and achieve the ultimate,
the Way must reach its utmost point,
then one can attain the beauty of Heaven and Earth.
"Yáo and Shùn Did Not Arbitrarily Transfer, Tāng and Wǔ Did Not Unjustly Kill - Chapter 25"
How could Yáo and Shùn arbitrarily transfer the world?
The words of the "Classic of Filial Piety" say:
"Serve one's father with filial piety,
thus serve Heaven with understanding."
Serving Heaven and one's father
follows the same ritual.
If a father gives something important to his son,
the son dare not arbitrarily give it to others,
all human hearts are like this;
then the king is also the son of Heaven,
Heaven gave the world to Yáo and Shùn,
Yáo and Shùn received the mandate from Heaven and ruled the world,
how could a son dare to arbitrarily give what he received importantly from Heaven to others?
Heaven does not gradually take away what it gave to Yáo and Shùn without cause,
clarifying the way of a son,
then Yáo and Shùn not privately passing on the world and arbitrarily transferring positions
is beyond doubt.
Confucians consider Tāng and Wǔ as the most worthy and great sages,
believing they fully embodied the Way, exhausted righteousness, and achieved perfect beauty,
thus ranking them with Yáo and Shùn,
calling them sage kings,
and following them as models;
now you consider Tāng and Wǔ unjust,
then what king of which era
is called righteous by you?
Said:
I do not know.
Not knowing,
do you think there are no righteous kings in the world?
Or are there righteous ones that you do not know?
Then answer with Shénnóng.
Respond by saying:
Did Shénnóng's reign as Son of Heaven
arise together with Heaven and Earth?
Or did he have campaigns to wage?
If Shénnóng had campaigns,
it is acceptable;
if Tāng and Wǔ had campaigns,
why alone is it unacceptable?
Why?
Moreover, Heaven gave birth to the people,
not for the king;
but Heaven established the king for the people.
Thus, those whose virtue is sufficient to comfort and delight the people,
Heaven grants them;
those whose wickedness is sufficient to harm the people,
Heaven takes it away.
The "Book of Songs" says:
"The officers of Yīn are elegant and swift,
performing the libation in Jīng,
they serve in Zhōu,
the Mandate of Heaven is not constant."
This says Heaven does not constantly grant,
nor constantly take away.
Thus, those who fēnged on Mount Tài,
shàned at Liángfù below,
changed surnames and became kings,
with virtue like Yáo and Shùn, were seventy-two persons,
kings are granted by Heaven,
those they campaign against,
are all taken away by Heaven,
now if only considering Tāng and Wǔ's campaigns against Jié and Zhòu as unjust,
then the seventy-two kings also had campaigns,
extending your argument,
would consider all seventy-two kings as unjust.
Thus, when Xià was without the Way, Yīn campaigned against it,
when Yīn was without the Way, Zhōu campaigned against it,
when Zhōu was without the Way, Qín campaigned against it,
when Qín was without the Way, Hàn campaigned against it.
Those with the Way campaign against those without,
this is the principle of Heaven,
which has existed for a long time!
How can it only apply to Tāng and Wǔ!
Those who criticize Tāng and Wǔ's campaigns against Jié and Zhòu,
would also criticize Qín's campaign against Zhōu,
not only do they not know Heaven's principle,
but also do not understand human ritual,
ritual requires a son to conceal his father's faults.
Now if campaigning is truly unjust,
one should conceal it for the state,
how can it be like slanderers,
this is what is called one word with double errors.
The ruler is one who holds commands,
commands are to be followed and prohibitions observed,
now Jié and Zhòu commanded the world but were not followed,
prohibited the world but not observed,
how can they be said to rule the world?
If they truly could not rule the world,
why speak of Tāng and Wǔ's regicide?
"Regulations on Attire - Chapter 26"
Taking one hundred sixty thousand states and dividing them into three,
then each measures rank to regulate attire,
assesses salary to use wealth.
Food and drink have measures,
clothing has regulations,
palaces and rooms have limits,
livestock and servants have numbers,
boats, carriages, armor, and tools have restrictions;
in life, there are distinctions for canopies, crowns, official robes, positions, noble salaries, fields, and residences,
in death, there are measures for inner and outer coffins, shrouds, and graves.
Even with worthy talent and fine physique,
without the rank,
one dare not wear its attire;
even with wealthy family and abundant assets,
without the salary,
one dare not use its wealth.
The Son of Heaven's attire has patterns,
ladies may not wear them in feasts or temples,
generals and great officers may not wear ministers' attire in feasts or temples,
generals and great officers wear them at court,
officials by command,
scholars stop at girdle trims.
Commoners dare not wear mixed colors,
artisans and merchants dare not wear fox or raccoon fur,
punished and disgraced people dare not wear silk, black, red, or ride horses,
this is called attire regulation.
"Regulations on Measures - Chapter 27"
Confucius said:
"Do not worry about poverty, but worry about inequality."
Thus, where there is accumulation and weight,
there is emptiness.
Great wealth leads to arrogance,
great poverty leads to worry.
Worry leads to theft,
arrogance leads to violence,
this is the nature of the masses.
The sage, from the nature of the masses,
sees where disorder arises,
thus establishes human ways and differentiates above and below,
so that the wealthy are sufficient to display nobility without becoming arrogant,
the poor are sufficient to sustain life without becoming worried,
using this as the measure to adjust and equalize,
thus wealth is not lacking and above and below are at peace,
so it is easy to govern.
Now the world abandons these measure regulations,
and each follows their desires.
Desires are endless,
and customs become self-indulgent,
the trend is limitless.
The great are troubled by insufficiency above,
and the common people are emaciated below,
then the wealthy increasingly covet profit and refuse to do righteousness,
the poor daily violate prohibitions and cannot be stopped,
this is why the world is difficult to govern.
Confucius said:
"The noble person does not exhaust profits but leaves them for the people."
The "Book of Songs" says:
"There they leave a handful,
here an unbound sheaf,
for the benefit of widows."
Thus, the noble person in office does not farm,
in fields does not fish,
when eating does not strive for delicacies,
great officers do not sit on sheep,
scholars do not sit on dogs.
The "Book of Songs" says:
"Gathering the mustard plant and the turnip,
do not reject the lower parts.
Do not violate virtuous words,
and I will die with you."
Using this to guard the people,
the people still forget righteousness and contend for profit,
to the point of losing their lives.
Heaven does not doubly grant,
having horns, one may not have upper teeth.
Thus, having the large,
one may not have the small,
this is Heaven's number.
If one already has the large,
and also takes the small,
Heaven cannot satisfy it,
let alone humans!
Thus, the wise sage imitates Heaven's actions to establish regulations,
so that those with high salaries
also may not take small profits or compete with the people for profit-making trades,
this is the principle of Heaven.
All sources of chaos
stem from subtle suspicions,
which gradually grow and expand until they become major issues.
The sages clarify what is doubtful,
distinguish what is subtle,
and eliminate what is delicate,
preventing suspicion
by taking early precautions.
The way of the sages
is akin to multiple dikes and defenses,
referred to as systems of regulation,
called rites and protocols.
Thus, nobles and commoners have their ranks,
clothing has its distinctions,
the court has its positions,
and the community has its order.
Then the people have grounds for deference and dare not contend,
which is the means to unify them.
The "Book of Documents" says:
"Those who wear robes have their duties;
who would dare not to yield?
Who would dare not to respond with respect?"
This is what it means.
All clothing is originally made
to cover the body and keep it warm.
Yet dyeing it with five colors and adorning it with patterns
is not to enhance the skin or the vitality of blood and energy,
but to honor the noble and respect the worthy,
and to clearly distinguish the hierarchy between superior and inferior,
ensuring that teachings are swiftly implemented,
and transformation is easily achieved,
all for the sake of governance.
If the regulatory systems are abandoned,
allowing everyone to follow their desires,
indulge their whims,
and chase after the limitless,
this would greatly disrupt human relations and waste resources,
losing the original intent behind the creation of ornate patterns.
If the hierarchy between superior and inferior is not distinguished,
the situation will be unmanageable,
hence suffering from chaos;
if coveted goods are unlimited,
their supply cannot meet demand,
hence suffering from poverty.
Now, to turn chaos into order
and poverty into prosperity,
it is imperative to revert to the systems and regulations.
In ancient times, the Son of Heaven wore patterned robes,
the feudal lords did not use them for casual wear,
the high officials received them as stipends,
but also did not use them for casual wear,
while commoners wore plain cloth,
this is the general outline.
"On Nobility and the State, Chapter Twenty-eight"
The Spring and Autumn Annals states:
"Met with the Prime Minister Zhōu."
It also says:
"The Duke met with the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Earl of Zhèng, Baron of Xǔ, and Viscount of Téng."
It further states:
"First offered six rows of dancers."
The Commentary says:
"The Three Dukes of the Son of Heaven are called 'Duke',
the descendants of former kings are called 'Duke',
other major states are called 'Marquis',
and minor states are called 'Earl', 'Viscount', 'Baron'."
There are five grades in total,
thus the Zhōu dynasty had five ranks of nobility,
and officials had three grades,
with more titles than actual power.
The Spring and Autumn Annals uses three grades,
combining Earl, Viscount, and Baron into one rank,
with officials in two grades,
having fewer titles but more substantial power.
The Spring and Autumn Annals states:
"Jīng."
The Commentary says:
"Clan name is inferior to personal name,
personal name is inferior to courtesy name,
courtesy name is inferior to style name."
There are four levels in total,
designated as attached territories,
shared by the Three Dynasties.
How then were their territories ranked?
It is said:
The Son of Heaven's capital domain spans a thousand lǐ,
Dukes and Marquises a hundred lǐ,
Earls seventy lǐ,
Viscounts and Barons fifty lǐ,
attached territories:
those with style names thirty lǐ square,
those with personal names twenty lǐ square,
those with clan names fifteen lǐ square.
The Spring and Autumn Annals states:
"Prime Minister Zhōu."
The Commentary says:
"One of the Three Dukes of the Son of Heaven."
"Jì Bó came."
The Commentary says:
"A senior official of the Son of Heaven."
"Prime Minister Qú Bó Jiū."
The Commentary says:
"A junior official."
"Shí Shàng."
The Commentary says:
"An officer of the Son of Heaven."
"Wáng rén."
The Commentary says:
"A minor official, referring to a lower officer."
There are five grades in total.
The Spring and Autumn Annals states:
"Established three armies."
The Commentary says:
"Why record this?
To criticize;
why criticize this?
In ancient times, there were senior ministers, junior ministers, senior officers, and junior officers."
There are four grades in total,
with senior officials of small states equivalent to junior ministers of medium states,
senior officials of medium states equivalent to junior ministers of large states,
and junior officials of large states equivalent to junior officers of the Son of Heaven.
There are twenty-four ranks,
with eight levels of emolument,
those with great merit and virtue receive high ranks and lands,
those with lesser merit and virtue receive lower ranks and lands,
the highly talented hold high offices,
the less talented receive lower positions,
each according to their ability,
this is the pinnacle of governance.
Thus, those who lead ten thousand are called Yīng (Elite),
those who lead a thousand are called Jùn (Outstanding),
those who lead a hundred are called Jié (Distinguished),
those who lead ten are called Háo (Prominent),
Háo, Jié, Jùn, and Yīng do not encroach upon each other,
thus governing the world is as easy as looking at one's palm.
By what method are these numbers determined?
It is said:
The Son of Heaven divides into five grades on left and right,
totaling three hundred sixty-three persons,
modeled after the number of days in a year.
It symbolizes the colors of the five seasons.
With additional senior and junior ministers totaling two hundred eighty persons,
representing the celestial court;
doubling the number of feudal lords.
Feudal lords have four external auxiliary ranks,
totaling one hundred twenty persons,
modeled after the numbers of the four seasons and sixty-day cycle.
With five additional auxiliaries,
and lower ranks,
totaling sixty persons,
modeled after the numbers of days and hours.
Why must auxiliaries be grouped in threes repeatedly?
Why?
It is said:
Three months form a season,
three hours form a sign.
Why do feudal lords have five ranks?
Why?
They model the numbers of heaven and earth.
The five offices follow the same principle.
How then are officials established,
and responsibilities divided?
It is said:
Large feudal states have four armies,
following ancient institutions,
with one army dedicated to the ducal house.
Why are there three armies per population?
Why?
It is said:
A large state has one hundred sixty thousand people,
supporting three armies.
How is this calculated?
It is said:
Based on the well-field system,
one square lǐ equals one well-field,
one well-field of nine hundred mǔ supports a population,
eight families per square lǐ,
each family farming one hundred mǔ,
feeding five persons.
Superior farmers cultivate one hundred mǔ,
feeding nine persons,
next grade eight persons,
next seven persons,
next six persons,
next five persons.
Balancing more and less,
averaging three persons per hundred mǔ,
twenty-four persons per square lǐ.
Ten square lǐ,
yield two hundred forty persons,
ten lǐ square equals one hundred square lǐ.
Yielding twenty-four thousand persons.
One hundred lǐ square equals one thousand square lǐ,
yielding two hundred forty thousand persons,
one thousand lǐ square equals ten thousand square lǐ,
yielding two million four hundred thousand persons,
then deducting one-third.
For city walls, moats, towns, houses, alleys, streets, markets, offices, gardens, and parks
leaving sixty-six ten-lǐ square fertile fields,
and sixty-six square lǐ,
fixed ratio yields one hundred sixty thousand persons.
Divided into three,
each being fifty-three thousand three hundred thirty persons,
forming three large armies.
This applies to Dukes and Marquises.
The Son of Heaven's territory spans a thousand lǐ square,
